item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 16, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Djibouti Abdoulkader Houssein Omar will pay an official visit to China from October 19 to 25. At the invitation of Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi, Minister of Foreign Affairs, La Francophonie and Congolese Abroad of the Republic of the Congo Constant-Serge Bounda will pay an official visit to China from October 19 to 25. People’s Daily: Tomorrow (October 17) is the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty. Global poverty reduction still faces many challenges from slowing growth, geopolitical conflicts, etc. A report jointly issued by the UN Development Programme and Oxford University shows that 1.2 billion people globally are living in multidimensional poverty. Comments say that China has made enormous contribution to global poverty reduction and provided invaluable experience for the Global South. What is China’s comment? Mao Ning: China has eradicated absolute poverty—a historic success— and realized the poverty reduction goal set by the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development 10 years in advance. These are results of China’s people-centered pragmatic actions, the determination to leave no one behind, and the perseverance to reach for the original goal. Eradicating poverty is a shared aspiration of all humanity. If China can succeed in this, other countries can succeed as well. China has made active efforts to promote poverty reduction cooperation. We have put poverty alleviation at the top of the eight priority areas of cooperation in the Global Development Initiative, helped Global South countries improve development resilience by sharing juncao and hybrid rice technology, and sent out thousands of experts for technical assistance. We have also initiated the establishment of the Global Partnership for Poverty Alleviation and Development to turn China’s practice and experience to global public goods that are useful in other countries. China will continue to enhance cooperation with the rest of the world to advance the poverty reduction process and achieve common development. Bloomberg: Even though China has compromised with the EU regarding its trade with the bloc and China has announced that it’s going to limit the number of hybrid car exports to the EU, there is a report that the EU is preparing new trade powers in order to reduce its trade deficit with China. Can you comment? Mao Ning: China-EU economic and trade relations are win-win in nature. The success of the recent second meeting of the China-EU Trade and Investment Consultation fully proves that the two sides can properly handle differences through dialogue. We hope that the EU will honor its commitments on freedom and openness, follow the WTO rules, steer clear of protectionist and discriminatory policies and measures, and walk toward the same direction with China to jointly promote the upward balance and sustainable development of China-EU trade, and keep the global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded. Al Araby Television Network: In his meeting with Israeli President Herzog in Azerbaijan, Foreign Minister Wang Yi stressed that the establishment of settlements in the West Bank must be stopped and reversed. He also stated that the Palestinian question is the greatest historical injustice of this century. Besides the expansion of settlements, settlers in the West Bank, backed by Israeli military and police forces, have been blatantly destroying Palestinians’ land and property—actions widely seen as an attempt to displace local Palestinians. Meanwhile, Palestinians in Gaza continue to face attacks, humanitarian aid remains difficult to deliver, and reconstruction of damaged facilities is progressing slowly. How does China view the current situation in Palestine? What concrete actions does China plan to take to address the injustice? Mao Ning: The Palestinian question lies at the heart of the Middle East issue, and the two-State solution is the fundamental way out of the Palestinian question. With persistent tensions in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, we believe that the regional conflict should not divert the international attention from the Palestinian question, the ceasefire agreement regarding Gaza must be effectively implemented, and humanitarian access must be guaranteed. Recently, President Xi Jinping put forward four principles for resolving the Palestinian question, namely upholding the two-State solution, upholding the principle of “Palestinians governing Palestine,” upholding humanitarianism, and upholding fairness and justice. These principles reflect China’s sense of responsibility as a major country regarding the Palestinian question and embody the international community’s call for justice. China will continue to stand on the side of international justice and, together with all peace-loving nations, firmly support the two-State solution and work for a comprehensive, just and lasting solution to the Palestinian question at an early date. CGTN: It’s reported that at a House of Representatives Budget Committee session on October 14, prime minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi said there was room to consider remarks made by former Foreign Minister Katsuya Okada suggesting that U.S. nuclear-armed vessels could be allowed to port in Japan during a crisis. She hinted at the possibility of explicitly stating exceptions to the three non-nuclear principles. Sanae Takaichi also said in response to Japan Innovation Party’s suggestion on introducing nuclear-powered submarines that her government will seriously consider the possibility in a concrete and realistic manner, in the face of increased military activity by its neighbors. The government will also take into account developments regarding nuclear-powered submarines in partner countries such as Australia and South Korea, she added. What’s your comment? Mao Ning: The remarks once again revealed Japanese authorities’ inflating ambitions of possessing nuclear weapons. The current Japanese administration has been turning a blind eye to its international obligations on non-proliferation, attempting to progressively ease nuclear restrictions, strengthen the so-called “extended deterrence” arrangement with its allies, ditch the three non-nuclear principles, and introduce nuclear-powered submarines, and even seeking to deploy nuclear weapons in Japan. Such moves pose a serious threat to peace and stability in Asia and the wider world. There is no room for consideration for Japan to follow the postwar international order and honor its international obligations. Japan should face up to the concerns of the international community, do serious soul-searching on Japanese militarists’ past crimes, abandon remilitarization and nuclear attempt, and not stand on the opposite side of the international community once again. Phoenix TV: To follow up on your remarks regarding Japan considering to introduce nuclear-powered submarines, we notice that Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi questioned China’s criticism against Japan, saying that countries that do not possess nuclear weapons or strategic bombers are being criticized by countries that possess both. What’s your comment? Mao Ning: As a WWII defeated nation and a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty, Japan is obligated under international law to refrain from breaching the exclusively defense-oriented policy and possessing nuclear weapons. It is high time that Japanese politicians caught up on history and law. Bloomberg: Indian finance minister said today that India is facing growing trade imbalances with China and blamed China’s non-tariff barriers as a reason why this trade deficit is widening. Can you respond? Mao Ning: I’d refer you to China’s competent authorities for the specific question. What I can tell you is that China never aims for trade surplus. We stand ready to work with India to address each other’s economic and trade concerns in a balanced way and promote the steady development of bilateral relations. China News Service: Following “China Travel” and “Chinamaxxing,” a new buzzword “China Haul” has been gaining traction on social media. Many foreign visitors arrive in China with empty suitcases and leave with them packed full of purchases. Unboxing videos pop up everywhere on the Internet. People in foreign cities like London and Paris are also flocking to local Chinese pop-up stores to shop. What’s your take on that? Mao Ning: It’s good to see that more and more foreign friends believe that China is worth a visit; Chinese brands are worth buying; and Chinese lifestyle is worth a try. That speaks to the vitality of Chinese market, the charm of Chinese people’s everyday life, and the appeal of China’s social convenience. China will keep its door wide open, and foster closer people-to-people bonds, so that more foreign friends can feel the pulse of China and fall in love with China. AFP: The new White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia said in an interview yesterday that China lacked “proper toilets.” In the interview, she said that back in 2016, there was a perception that China was set to overtake the U.S. However, she said that this would not have been possible because “China didn’t even have proper toilets.” Have you noticed these remarks by the White House Press Secretary and do you have any comment on these remarks? Mao Ning: She’s welcome to come and see China when she has the opportunity. Reuters: China’s ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan said that China “may easily win” in a confrontation between the two countries although China would not use force. This was in reaction to the Philippine defence secretary calling China a regional troublemaker. Philippine President also said that the Chinese ambassador’s remarks sounded like a threat. Does the foreign ministry have any comment? (Similar question from Kyodo News) Mao Ning: China’s position on improving and growing its ties with the Philippines is clear. It is hoped that the Philippine side will have a full and accurate understanding of it. DPA: U.S. President Donald Trump said that Washington is holding talks with Russia and China on denuclearization. Can China confirm talks with the U.S. side on this? Mao Ning: China has made clear its position on this on multiple occasions. Sitting on an enormous nuclear arsenal, the U.S. should fulfill its special and primary responsibility for nuclear disarmament. This is the international consensus. China’s nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the U.S. and Russia. It is neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 15, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
At the invitation of Prime Minister of the Republic of Uzbekistan Abdulla Aripov, Premier of the State Council Li Qiang will pay an official visit to Uzbekistan from October 17 to 18. At the invitation of Prime Minister of the Republic of Tajikistan Kokhir Rasulzoda, Premier Li Qiang will pay an official visit to Tajikistan from October 18 to 20 and attend the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO). At the invitation of Prime Minister of the Russian Federation Mikhail Mishustin, Premier Li Qiang will travel to Russia from October 20 to 22 for the 31st regular meeting between Chinese and Russian heads of government. Xinhua News Agency: You just announced that Premier Li Qiang will visit Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, and attend the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization. He will also travel to Russia for the 31st regular meeting between Chinese and Russian heads of government. Can you share the background and China’s expectation? Mao Ning: China and Uzbekistan are all-weather comprehensive strategic partners for the new era. Over recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, China-Uzbekistan relations have entered a golden period with stronger mutual trust and fruitful cooperation in various areas. In August this year, the two presidents met in Bishkek where they made new strategic planning for the future development of bilateral relations. China and Tajikistan are friendly neighbors and comprehensive strategic cooperative partners for the new era. Since the two countries established diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have maintained a sound and steady momentum of growth. In May this year, President Xi Jinping met with President Emomali Rahmon who was on a state visit to China. The two sides signed and issued the treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation, providing a firm safeguard for the ever-lasting friendship between the two countries. China hopes the visit will galvanize efforts of all three countries to accelerate the implementation of the important common understandings between the presidents, deepen political mutual trust, expand mutually-beneficial cooperation, promote common development, and provide new impetus for building the China-Uzbekistan and China-Tajikistan community with a shared future. This year marks the 30th anniversary of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation. President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin have met twice this year, guiding bilateral relations into a new stage with higher-quality and faster development. Premier Li Qiang’s attendance at the 31st regular meeting between Chinese and Russian heads of government will serve as an opportunity for the two countries to work together to deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents, deepen political mutual trust, and enhance and substantiate all-round practical cooperation for the benefit of the two peoples. The SCO is in its 25th year now. At the successful SCO Summit in Bishkek not long ago, leaders of member states reached important common understandings on carrying forward the Shanghai Spirit under the new circumstances, promoting SCO’s development and cooperation, and improving the global governance system. President Xi Jinping made an in-depth elaboration on the core tenets of an equal and orderly multipolar world, put forward new initiatives on practical cooperation, and charted the course for high-quality development of the SCO. At the upcoming meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of the SCO in Dushanbe, Premier Li Qiang will have in-depth exchanges of views with various parties on implementing the strategic blueprint of the SCO Tianjin Summit and the outcome consensus of the SCO Bishkek Summit, so as to better protect the shared interests of member states and make SCO’s contribution to peace, stability, development and prosperity of the region and beyond. Bloomberg: Can you confirm a report that China has agreed to restructure some of Zimbabwe’s debt? This is according to Zimbabwe’s finance minister, but we haven’t heard anything about this from China. Mao Ning: China and Zimbabwe are traditional friends. The Chinese side attaches high importance to Zimbabwe’s debt treatment request. The competent authorities and financial institutions of both sides are in communication over this. For more updates, I would refer you to the competent Chinese authorities. AFP: Yesterday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with his Russian counterpart Mr. Lavrov in Baku, Azerbaijan. According to a statement from the Russian foreign ministry, Mr. Lavrov presented Mr. Wang Yi with a report. This report states that the Ukrainian authorities orchestrated the killings in Bucha in 2022 and then blamed Russian troops for them. Can you confirm whether Mr. Lavrov did in fact give a copy of this report to Mr. Wang? Maybe can you just reiterate what’s China’s position on this Bucha incident? Is it the same as Russia’s position? Mao Ning: We have released a readout on the meeting between Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his Russian counterpart. I don’t have anything further to add. Global Times: Japanese media recently disclosed for the first time internal meeting minutes of the Yasukuni war shrine revealing the decision-making process of the enshrinement of 14 Class-A war criminals including Hideki Tojo. It shows that the Japanese government made arrangements on the enshrinement of Class-A war criminals with the shrine in as early as the 1960s, but chose to keep the public in the dark until it was revealed in 1979. What’s China’s comment? Mao Ning: The documents proved once again that the Japanese government at the time knew full well the disgrace of enshrining Class-A war criminals and, fearful of the consequences, deliberately kept the decision-making process secret. These Class-A war criminals were the chief culprits behind Japanese militarists’ war of aggression with the blood of innumerable war victims on their hands. The solemn verdict of the Tokyo Trials condemned them to perpetual infamy, thereby upholding international justice and laying the legal foundation for the postwar international order. Yet those running the Japanese government have again and again paid respects to what is in fact a shrine to war criminals. One has to ask: where has the conscience gone? History shall not be rewritten. Truth shall not be erased. Japan committed undeniable crimes during its militarist aggression. Those running the Japanese government must face history squarely, reflect on the war crimes, and make a genuine break with its militarist past.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 14, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14
Kyodo News: It’s reported that Russia said a delegation from China’s Heilongjiang Province yesterday visited the Northern Territories of Japan. What’s China’s comment? Mao Ning: A delegation from Heilongjiang Province recently visited Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, capital of Russia’s Sakhalin Oblast, a sister province of Heilongjiang, for friendly exchanges. I will not comment on business activities conducted by private companies during the visit. CGTN: The 140th China Import and Export Fair is about to open, and the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) will be launched on November 5. Most recently, China has successfully held the China International Fair for Trade in Services, the China-ASEAN Expo and the Global Digital Trade Expo. Media comments say that these events drew active participation from global businesses and provide important impetus for global economy and trade. What is your comment? Mao Ning: These expos you mentioned are important windows on China’s global connectedness and how it enables development and delivers for the people across the world. The China Import and Export Fair is in its 70th year now and this year’s fair is expected to host some 32,000 businesses. More than 11,000 of them either possess specialized and sophisticated technologies for producing novel and unique products or are leaders in specific fields. This year’s CIIE will continue to provide free exhibition stands for least developed countries. There will be an upgraded Asia-Africa Products Zone, where African countries having diplomatic relations with China in particular can make full use of the “zero tariff” treatment. Underpinning the strong appeal of these expos are China’s determination and efforts to advance high-standard opening up and share development opportunities with the world. Reuters: Xinhua reported today that the New Yalu River Bridge that links China and North Korea will be open from tomorrow. How much increase in trade does China expect from this land connection? Also about tourism, what are the expectations? There are reports in North Korea saying the bridge is only open for cargo. Is this true? Mao Ning: As agreed between China and the DPRK, the New Yalu River Bridge connecting the two countries will officially open to traffic on October 15, and a joint ceremony will be held tomorrow to mark the inauguration. China and the DPRK are friendly neighbors linked by mountains and rivers. The New Yalu River Bridge will serve as an important infrastructure for bilateral connectivity and further facilitate the economic, trade and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries and contribute to the welfare of the two peoples. AFP: On this Chinese delegation’s visit to this island held by Russia and claimed by Japan, the Japanese foreign minister said today it is absolutely unacceptable that third countries enter and operate on these islands. He said Japan yesterday conveyed its position to China through diplomatic channels. What’s your response to this message by Japan? Mao Ning: I’ve shared information on the visit of the delegation from Heilongjiang Province. China believes the outcomes of the victory of the World Anti-Fascist War must always be respected and upheld. Reuters: Following up on the New Yalu River Bridge, can we know what are the details of the opening ceremony tomorrow? What time is it happening and who can be expected to be there? Mao Ning: There will be timely updates on the inauguration ceremony. Please stay tuned. AFP: The Taiwanese authorities said today they will inject up to US$ 4.4 billion into a U.S. pipeline project in Alaska. Given the huge amount of this investment, I wonder if the foreign ministry has any comment or any view on the deal. Mao Ning: External exchanges of China’s Taiwan region must be handled in line with the one-China principle. The DPP authorities will not succeed in seeking “Taiwan independence” in the name of trade and investment.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 13, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
People’s Daily: It is reported that India’s Ministry of Home Affairs made a statement in which it claimed that the standardized names of 28 places have been identified and marked on the official map after the consultation with the local government of Ladakh. Some press mentioned that some of the places lie in the disputed region under China’s actual control. What is China’s comment? Mao Ning: China has never recognized the so-called “Union Territory of Ladakh” unilaterally and illegally established by India, and firmly opposes the so-called “standardized names” publicized by India. This move by India is illegal and void and does not change the fact that the western sector of the China-India boundary belongs to China. The Paper: It is reported that at a ceremony held by the Ministry of Investment and Downstream Industry and the Indonesia Weda Bay Industrial Park to launch Chinese-backed mining downstream projects, President Prabowo thanked Chinese investors for the partnership and trust, and emphasized that the Indonesian government considers those who believe in Indonesia, those who dare to collaborate in new areas with Indonesia, as brothers and sisters. Indonesia will protect its partners as brothers. What’s China comment? Mao Ning: China appreciates the remarks made by the Indonesian leadership. Over the years, China and Indonesia have deepened mutually beneficial cooperation in energy, mining and other areas by drawing on each other’s strengths, which has brought tangible benefits to our two countries and peoples. The success of Chinese companies in Indonesia is Indonesia’s success too. China will work with Indonesia to follow through the strategic common understanding of the two presidents and continue to deepen mutually beneficial cooperation in relevant fields, so as to better support Indonesia in transforming its resource advantages into momentum for development and contribute to Indonesia’s prosperity. We are confident that the Indonesian government will continue to protect Chinese companies’ legitimate rights and interests and provide an open, fair, transparent and friendly business environment. AFP: The International Monetary Fund lowered its forecasts for China’s economic growth this year to 4.5% on Tuesday. This comes as higher energy prices due to the Middle East conflict and a domestic spending slump weigh on activity. I wonder if the foreign ministry has a comment on the IMF’s assessment and forecast? Mao Ning: I’d refer you to competent authorities. Let me say that the fundamentals sustaining China’s sound economic growth in the long run remain unchanged, and we are confident in China’s economic prospect. CCTV: Following the moving reunion of Ms. Yin Yuzhen and her American friend Mr. Ronald Sakolsky who worked together to combat desertification, which touched many people in both China and the United States. Recently, we have also read about an American named David Victor Plymire and his connection to Huangyuan County, Qinghai Province. His story has gained a lot of attention as well. Can you share more information on that? Mao Ning: People-to-people friendship between China and the United States is jointly forged by ordinary people from both countries. The 95-year-old Mr. Plymire you mentioned lived in Huangyuan County, Qinghai Province for 17 years, and regards the place as his hometown. Mr. Plymire has helped donate medical equipment to Huangyuan County, provided financial aid for local education, and facilitated training opportunities in the U.S. for the county’s English teachers. He once humbly said that all he has done is simply “fulfilling my duty to my own family.” His story has touched many people. People-to-people friendship holds the key to state-to-state relations. The exchanges between the Chinese and American people are like small streams that ultimately converge to form the vast river of China-U.S. friendship. China will continue to support people-to-people exchanges between the two countries and contribute to building a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity. Reuters: The U.S. embassy in Fiji said on Monday that hackers linked to China compromised a regional organization’s network based in Fiji. Does China have any comment on that? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with the specifics. Let me say that China firmly opposes and combats hacking activities in accordance with the law. That said, we reject vilification against China under the pretext of cybersecurity. Beijing Youth Daily: It’s reported that Professor Colin Mackerras, renowned Australian sinologist who received the Chinese Government Friendship Award, passed away a few days ago after illness. Do you have any comment? Mao Ning: Professor Colin Mackerras was long committed to the friendly ties between Australia and China, and made important contribution to enhancing mutual understanding and friendship between the Chinese and Australian people. We deeply mourn for the passing of Professor Mackerras and our thoughts are with his family. Bloomberg: President Donald Trump said that he does not believe Russia and China are helping Iran. Could you comment on that? Mao Ning: China has made clear its position on this issue more than once. We will continue working with relevant countries and the international community to make constructive efforts for restoring peace, stability and development in the Middle East. Reuters: The Trump administration via the U.S. State Department recently said that it opposes “coercion and aggression” by China against countries for exercising their sovereign rights. It said this in response to Beijing sanctioning ministers from Belize and Paraguay over their ties to Taiwan. Do you have any comment? Mao Ning: The one-China principle is a basic norm in international relations and prevailing international consensus. It is also the political foundation of China-U.S. relations. The U.S. needs to abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiqués, handle the Taiwan question prudently, and stop sending wrong signals to “Taiwan independence” separatist forces.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 12, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Minister of Foreign Affairs Wang Yi will attend the Seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) held in Baku, Azerbaijan on October 15 as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping, and visit Azerbaijan, Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria from October 14 to 20. Beijing Daily: Today, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs put on its website the decision to take countermeasures against Paraguay’s Minister of Information and Communication Technologies Gustavo Emigdio Villate Samaniego and Belize Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Francis Fonseca. Could you share more information on that? Mao Ning: The Taiwan question is a major issue of principle bearing on China’s sovereignty and national reunification. It is at the core of China’s core interests. Certain politicians in Paraguay and Belize willingly serve as chess pieces for the DPP authorities in their pursuit of independence by soliciting external support. Their visits to Taiwan and reception of “Taiwan independence” separatist forces in their countries constitute severe interference in China’s internal affairs. They also attacked and smeared China by spreading the “Chinese cyber attack” disinformation, causing egregious impact in the world. In response to these moves and in accordance with the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law of the People’s Republic of China, China announced in the form of MFA decree countermeasures as an action of warning and deterrence. China News Service: Foreign Minister Wang Yi will attend the Seventh CICA Summit as Special Representative of President Xi Jinping and visit Azerbaijan. What’s China’s expectation of the visit? Mao Ning: CICA is an important mechanism for security dialogue and cooperation in Asia. Since its inception, CICA has been committed to enhancing interaction and confidence-building among countries and made important contribution to security, stability and development in the region. With growing complexity and volatility in the international and regional landscapes, Asian countries are increasingly keen to ensure peace and tranquility and promote economic growth. At the upcoming summit, China will engage in extensive dialogue and consultation with various parties to practice multilateralism, actively implement the four global initiatives, and enhance Asian governance, so as to make new contribution to building an Asian community with a shared future. China and Azerbaijan are comprehensive strategic partners. In recent years, under the strategic planning and guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Ilham Aliyev, China-Azerbaijan relations have maintained strong momentum of growth, with ever-deepening political mutual trust, steady progress in Belt and Road cooperation and fruitful collaboration on international affairs. This will be Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s first official visit to Azerbaijan in seven years. He will hold talks with Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov. We believe the visit will help fully implement the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state and deliver new outcomes for bilateral cooperation across various fields. AFP: U.S. President Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” between Ukraine and Russia on Sunday. The ceasefire was met with surprise from Kiev and silence from Moscow and appeared shaky as Russia appeared to strike multiple Ukrainian power plants on Sunday. Does the foreign ministry have a comment on this “energy ceasefire”? Mao Ning: China’s position on the Ukraine crisis is consistent and clear. We believe that dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out, and support all efforts conducive to peace. Reuters: The U.S. State Department last week said China’s maritime activities off Taiwan’s east coast are “deeply destabilizing.” What is the foreign ministry’s comment on that? Mao Ning: China has on multiple occasions made clear its position on this. China has exclusive economic zone and continental shelf in waters east of the Taiwan island. It is fully within China’s sovereign rights and jurisdiction, therefore legitimate, lawful and beyond reproach, for China to carry out activities in these waters. The party that instigates troubles and disrupts stability in this part of waters has never been the Chinese side. The Taiwan question is China’s internal affair that brooks no external interference. The U.S. needs to abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiqués, handle the Taiwan question prudently, and take concrete actions to uphold the overall China-U.S. relations and peace and stability in the region. Xinhua News Agency: On October 10, leader of the Taiwan region Lai Ching-te made a speech in which he again solicited external support for “Taiwan independence,” and smeared Chinese mainland. What’s your comment? Mao Ning: There is but one China in the world. Taiwan is an inalienable part of China’s territory, and the Government of the People’s Republic of China is the sole legal government representing the whole of China. To uphold the one-China principle, reject “Taiwan independence” separatist activities and support China’s reunification is where international public opinion trends. Lai Ching-te’s so-called “democracy” cannot hide his “Taiwan independence” separatist nature. Taiwan’s return to China is an integral part of the outcome of WWII victory and the postwar international order. The real status quo across the Taiwan Strait is that both sides of the Strait belong to one and the same China. Whatever Lai Ching-te says or does, it does not change the fact backed by history and law that Taiwan belongs to China or the doomed failure of “Taiwan independence,” and will by no means stop China’s ultimate reunification. CGTN: Could you elaborate on the program and China’s expectation of Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s visit to Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria? Mao Ning: Croatia, Montenegro and Bulgaria are China’s important cooperation partners in Southeastern Europe. In recent years, China has maintained close exchanges with the three countries. Notable results have been achieved in cooperation on economy and trade, investment, tourism and infrastructure. There is extensive common ground on safeguarding multilateralism, tackling global challenges, growing China-Europe relations and other topics. During the visit, Foreign Minister Wang Yi will hold talks with the foreign ministers of the three countries and have in-depth exchange of views with their leaders. Croatia is China’s important partner in the EU. The Chinese-built Pelješac Bridge is a landmark project of China-Croatia and China-EU cooperation. The two countries have enjoyed a more mature and stable partnership of comprehensive cooperation. Through the visit, China looks to better synergize development strategies and expand practical cooperation with Croatia, so as to promote the steady and sustained growth of bilateral ties. This year marks the 20th anniversary of China’s diplomatic relations with Montenegro. Throughout those two decades, the two sides have always treated each other with respect and as equals. Together, the two countries have built a series of landmark projects, such as the South-North Expressway in Montenegro. China hopes that through the Chinese foreign minister’s first visit, the two sides will expand the breadth and depth of mutually beneficial cooperation, carry forward the traditional friendship, and inject new impetus into bilateral relations for the next 20 years. Bulgaria is the second country in the entire world to establish diplomatic relations with New China. In recent years, China-Bulgaria strategic partnership has grown steadily, with close high-level exchanges and fruitful outcomes of practical cooperation. Through this visit, China looks to cement mutual trust, advance cooperation and deepen friendship with the new Bulgarian government, so as to further advance and deepen bilateral ties. Reuters: Regarding China’s sanctions on the Paraguay and Belize ministers, would this be first of such measures against ministers from countries that maintain ties with Taiwan? Mao Ning: For diehard supporters of “Taiwan independence” separatist forces, China will take all necessary punitive measures to firmly safeguard national sovereignty and territorial integrity. We urge the very few countries left which still have so-called “diplomatic ties” with China’s Taiwan region to avoid being repeatedly manipulated and used by separatist forces for “Taiwan independence.” Betting on “Taiwan independence” has no future. It will only cost them opportunities for development and lead to international isolation. Global Times: Following his recent visit to China, former Japanese Foreign Minister and head of the Japanese Association for the Promotion of International Trade Mr. Takeshi Iwaya said that the deterioration in China-Japan relations was caused by the Japanese side and that the Japanese government should seek ways to improve the bilateral ties. There are voices in Japan criticizing the evasion of historical responsibility for leading astray Japan’s policy toward China, and calling on the Japanese government to face up to and address the wrongdoings. What’s China’s comment? Mao Ning: China commends these remarks, which reflect reason and conscience among those with insight in Japan. As they have pointed out, the real issue lies in the distorted and erroneous views toward history and China held by those running the Japanese government, which has severely undermined the political foundation of China-Japan relations. The situation does not serve the two countries’ interests, and the responsibility rests fully with Japan. To bring China-Japan relations back to the right track, the ball is, apparently, in Japan’s court. We urge those running the Japanese government to heed and take seriously the just voice at home, face up to the root causes of the problem, abide by the four political documents between China and Japan, and genuinely reflect on and correct wrongdoings on such issues as Taiwan, the history, and their China perception. AFP: A fresh Houthis strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, killing one person and wounding 11 others. This comes a day after another deadly attack claimed by the Yemeni group. Can the Chinese foreign ministry comment on this? Mao Ning: China condemns the attacks, which caused significant casualties, and expresses grave concern over the escalating conflict. China opposes attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. We urge the parties concerned to refrain from actions that could further escalate regional tensions, resolve differences and disputes through dialogue and negotiations, and work toward peace and stability in the region at an early date. Shenzhen TV: Today is the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Papua New Guinea. How does China see the development of bilateral ties over the past 50 years? What’s China’s expectation moving forward? Mao Ning: Today marks the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between China and Papua New Guinea. President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang have respectively exchanged congratulatory messages with Governor-General Bob Dadae and Prime Minister James Marape. As President Xi pointed out in his congratulatory message, over half a century since the establishment of diplomatic ties, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, conducted fruitful cooperation for mutual benefit, and expanded people-to-people exchanges. The remarkable progress in bilateral relations has not only benefited the two peoples, but also injected strong momentum to building a community with a shared future between China and Pacific Island countries. China stands ready to work with Papua New Guinea to jointly implement the important common understandings reached between the two leaders, carry forward our traditional friendship, and strengthen exchanges and cooperation across the board, so as to elevate our comprehensive strategic partnership to new heights and build an even closer community with a shared future between China and Pacific Island countries. Reuters: There was a landslide in Nepal’s Gorkha district that led to the downstream flooding in the Budhi Gandaki river. This area is part of a major trekking route. Were there any Chinese nationals affected by the flood? Mao Ning: We have no information on Chinese casualties for the time being. We extend sympathies to Nepal, and will provide assistance within our capacity in light of Nepal’s need. AFP: The United States on Friday imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court, vowing to cripple its operations just hours after the Nobel Peace Prize went to a former ICC judge. I wonder if China has a comment on this. Mao Ning: We noticed the developments. China is not a state party to the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court. China’s position on relevant issues is consistent. AFP: South Korea’s military said that North Korea on Monday fired multiple ballistic missiles off its east coast. I wonder if the foreign ministry has a comment on this. Mao Ning: We notice relevant reports, and have no comment to add. Reuters: There have been youth-led protests happening in Delhi over the weekend and in several other cities in India as well, calling for the resignation of India’s election chief. Will China consider issuing any travel advisories against visiting Delhi or any part of India in the near future? Mao Ning: China noted the developments, and will assess whether advisories are needed as the situation evolves.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on the 7.6 Magnitude Earthquake in Panama
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Q: It’s reported that a 7.6 magnitude earthquake struck Panama on October 10, followed by over 100 aftershocks. What is China’s comment? A: China expresses sympathies to the Panamanian government and people in the affected region. As of now, there is no report of casualties involving Chinese nationals in the earthquake. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Chinese Embassy in Panama will continue to closely monitor the situation and promptly provide necessary assistance to Chinese nationals in need. We remind Chinese nationals in Panama to take precautions against secondary hazards caused by the earthquake.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 9, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
At the invitation of President Xi Jinping, President of the Republic of Botswana Duma Gideon Boko will pay a state visit to China from October 12 to 17. China News Service: You just announced the upcoming visit by President Boko. Could you please share the program of the visit and China’s expectations? How does China view the current China-Botswana relations? Mao Ning: The upcoming visit will mark President Boko’s first visit to China since assuming office. During the visit, President Xi will host a welcoming ceremony and a banquet for President Boko, and the two heads of state will hold talks. Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji will meet with him respectively. President Boko will also visit Fujian Province. China and Botswana are strategic partners. Over the 51 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the two countries have upheld sincere friendship and mutually beneficial cooperation. We support each other on major issues concerning respective core interests, assist each other in times of disaster and epidemic, join hands on the journey toward modernization, and firmly stand on the right side of history on international affairs. We are confident that the upcoming visit will elevate China-Botswana relations to a new height and further contribute to building an all-weather China-Africa community with a shared future for the new era. Shenzhen TV: It was reported that a spokesperson of the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) alleged that yesterday morning, under the firing of water cannons and dangerous maneuvers and disruptions from China Coast Guard, the PCG completed a medical evacuation mission for an injured personnel from the military vessel “grounded” at Ren’ai Jiao. What is China’s comment? Mao Ning: The spokesperson of China Coast Guard has issued a statement to share information on what actually happened. Yesterday morning, a Philippine Coast Guard vessel, without China’s permission, intruded the adjacent waters of Ren’ai Jiao, Nansha Qundao of China. China Coast Guard took legitimate and reasonable measures to handle the situation in accordance with laws and regulations. After communication between the two sides, out of humanitarian considerations, China gave timely permission to the Philippine side to evacuate injured personnel by small boat and provided necessary facilitation. Instead of acknowledging China’s facilitation, individual Philippine officials have distorted facts and wrongfully accused China without showing the whole picture to the public. This once again reveals their intention of provoking China and staging publicity stunts, which is rather despicable. China will not waver in responding to any provocation and safeguarding territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests. Reuters: U.S. officials from the Department of Justice said they seized seven internet domains that were linked to Chinese hackers that were trying to hack the U.S. and foreign critical infrastructure systems. Does China have a comment? Mao Ning: China firmly opposes and combats hacking activities in accordance with law. China also firmly opposes spreading disinformation and making noises for political agenda. Cybersecurity is an issue of common concern for China and the U.S. We urge the U.S. side to quit double standards and political manipulation, jointly tackle cybersecurity risks through equal-footed dialogue and consultation, and build a relationship characterized by peace, stability and mutual respect on cyber issues. AFP: China and the United States have reportedly discussed carrying out reciprocal visits to nuclear sites with plans to talk about this further in coming months. This is according to CNN based on sources familiar with the matter. Can the foreign ministry confirm this? Is China open to conducting reciprocal nuclear site visits with the United States? Mao Ning: The relevant report is not true. Phoenix TV: It’s been disclosed that Japan’s right-wing forces are making continuous efforts to tamper WWII history by entering adulterated data into mainstream AI models, some of which produce outputs with a clearly misguided view of history. For instance, they refer to the July 7 Incident as a “clash” between Japanese and Chinese troops, the Nanjing Massacre as the “Fall of Nanjing” and Japan’s aggression against Southeast Asia as “interest” in the region’s resources. What’s your comment? Mao Ning: Japan committed ironclad and undeniable crimes during militarist aggression. Using new technologies to poison the data is the latest method by Japanese right-wing forces to distort and glorify Japan’s war history. The aim is to embed a wrong perception of WWII history and misguide public opinion, so that Japan can break free from the postwar pacifist constraint and accelerate remilitarization. AI should be used for the positive and for good, not for tampering with historical facts and whitewashing war crimes. The covert moves of Japanese right-wing forces greatly hurt the sentiments of Japan’s war victims and constitute a blatant affront to human conscience. The international community must stay on high alert and push back those moves.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 8, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
At the invitation of Premier of the State Council Li Qiang, President of the Council of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé will pay an official visit to China from October 9 to 16. French President’s Diplomatic Adviser Emmanuel Bonne will be in China from October 9 to 13. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs Wang Yi will hold a new round of China-France Strategic Dialogue with him. Xinhua News Agency: To follow up on President of the Council of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé’s visit to China, can you share the program of the visit and China’s expectations? How does China view its relations with Togo? Mao Ning: President of the Council Faure is an old friend of China. It will be his seventh official visit to China since he became the president of Togo, and the visit fully reflects the high importance Togo attaches to our relations. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will meet with him, and Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji will hold talks and meet with him respectively. President Faure will also visit Shaanxi, Fujian, and Guangdong. China and Togo are comprehensive strategic partners. Since our diplomatic relations were established 54 years ago, our traditional friendship has been growing stronger with time. We firmly support each other on issues related to core interests and major concerns, with fruitful exchanges and cooperation across the board, setting a stellar example of equal treatment between big and small countries and solidarity and cooperation in the Global South. We believe that this visit will bring China-Togo relations to a new height and contribute to building an all-weather China-Africa community with a shared future for the new era. NHK: It was reported that in the meeting between the Chinese and U.S. presidents, President Trump asked the Chinese side to engage in dialogue with Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi and lift export controls against Japan. Is this true? Did the two sides talk about Japan in the meeting? If so, what was discussed? Mao Ning: China has released readouts on the meeting between the Chinese and U.S. presidents, which you may refer to. CRI: Russian Presidential Aide and Chairman of the Maritime Board Nikolai Patrushev is now in China for his visit. Can you brief us with relevant arrangements of this visit? What is China’s comment on current China-Russia relations? Mao Ning: China and Russia are comprehensive strategic partners of coordination for the new era. Under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin, recent years have seen deepened political mutual trust, closer strategic coordination and continuously expanding cooperation that is mutually beneficial between China and Russia. The two sides have set a fine example of a new type of international relations and relations between neighboring major countries. This is the first visit to China that Patrushev has made in the capacity of the Chairman of the Maritime Board of Russia. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs Wang Yi and other department chiefs will meet with Chairman Patrushev respectively to exchange views on bilateral relations and cooperation on maritime affairs. China is ready to take this visit as an opportunity to work with Russia to deepen strategic communication, promote practical cooperation, and keep injecting new momentum of development into China-Russia relations in the new era. CCTV: On October 5, the 63rd session of the Human Rights Council adopted in Geneva by consensus a resolution proposed by China, on behalf of 53 countries, titled “Promoting accessibility for the full enjoyment of all human rights by all.” Could you share more details on that? Mao Ning: Building a barrier-free environment is consistent with the vision of ensuring support for persons with disabilities and the elderly, and provides important safeguards for enabling all groups to participate equally and conveniently in social life and fully enjoy all human rights. Many countries commended China’s efforts to promote the vision of “accessibility for all,” and believes that it serves the real and pressing needs of developing countries to call for more technical assistance to developing countries and greater international cooperation in relevant fields. In 2024, the Human Rights Council adopted the resolution with the same title proposed by China. This was the first resolution specifically on accessibility. The adoption of this resolution a few days ago is of great significance for international community to promote and protect the human rights of all groups, actively address population ageing, leverage AI and other emerging technologies to facilitate information exchange on accessibility, and strengthen global governance and standard-setting in relevant areas. China will follow the guidance of the four global initiatives proposed by President Xi Jinping, and deepen its cooperation with various parties to earnestly implement the vision of “accessibility for all,” improve global governance on human rights, and promote sound progress of the international human rights cause. Reuters: Sources have told Reuters that China plans to put forward senior public health official Song Li as candidate for the top position at the World Health Organization. One of the sources said the planned nomination was a sign that China wanted to fill a void where the U.S. has stepped back at the WHO. Can the ministry share if China has indeed such nomination plans? And if so, is the U.S.’s withdrawal from UN agencies, such as WHO, a good opportunity for China to step in? Mao Ning: As the UN specialized agency for health, the WHO plays a leading and coordinating role in global public health governance. At present, multilateralism is facing severe challenges, and the development of global public health remains a long-term and arduous task. Amid the changing landscape and new circumstances, the Director-General has a crucial role to play in ensuring the WHO’s steady and sustained progress. China’s decision to nominate Doctor Song Li as candidate for the WHO Director-General reflects China’s aspiration to work with all parties for a global community of health for all, and demonstrates China’s firm support for multilateralism and the WHO. We believe that if Doctor Song Li is elected, it will help the WHO play a more positive role in promoting the health and wellbeing of all humanity. CGTN: Regarding the French President’s Diplomatic Adviser Emmanuel Bonne’s visit to China, can you provide the program and China’s expectation? Mao Ning: During the French President’s Diplomatic Adviser Emmanuel Bonne’s visit to China, he and Director Wang Yi will hold a new round of China-France Strategic Dialogue to have strategic communication on deepening China-France cooperation in different areas and in-depth exchange of views on international and regional issues of mutual interest. Last December, President Emmanuel Macron made his fourth state visit to China, during which the two heads-of-state had long, in-depth talks and reached important common understandings regarding strengthening China-France strategic communication, staying committed to openness and cooperation, jointly upholding multilateralism and so on. Through this dialogue, China expects to strengthen coordination and collaboration with France on bilateral and multilateral issues and promote the steady development of China-France and China-Europe relations. Global Times: It is reported that on October 1, the Tokyo District Court conducted the first public trial of Kodai Murata, a former officer of Japan’s Self-Defense Forces who illegally entered the Chinese embassy in Japan. Murata confessed to illegally entering the embassy with a knife without reservation but denied the charge of criminal intimidation. What is China’s comment? Mao Ning: It is shockingly malignant for a sitting Japanese SDF officer to break into the Chinese embassy carrying a knife and threaten Chinese diplomatic personnel with violence. This incident seriously violates the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, gravely threatens the safety and security of Chinese diplomatic personnel and premises, and exposes deep-seated problems in Japan, including the rampant spread of right-wing impact and lack of supervision and discipline in the SDF. Whether Japan can deal with the matter seriously in accordance with the law will test the Japanese government’s ability to fulfill its obligations under the international law and affect Japan’s credibility and reputation in the world. We once again urge Japan to bring the perpetrator to account and prevent similar incidents from happening again. Bloomberg: There are reports that Germany’s president is going to be visiting China. Could you confirm that and let us know the schedule and the list of Chinese leaders he will meet? Mao Ning: Regarding your question, I have no information to share at the moment. AFP: The European commissioner for trade begins two days of talks in Beijing today to avoid a trade escalation. What are China’s expectations in this regard and what message would you send to the European commissioner? Mao Ning: I would refer you to China’s competent authorities for anything specific. China always believes that it serves the shared interests of China and the EU to stay committed to openness and cooperation, and resolve economic and trade disputes through equal-footed dialogue and consultation. Reuters: Crowdstrike said in a report on Wednesday that an unidentified actor behind alleged cyber attacks on South Korean financial institutions used China-developed AI penetration testing tool, Chinese language prompt, as well as have left material suggesting possible links to China, including references to Guangdong and a Chinese university. Does China have any comment on this case or comment on any of the growing risks of Chinese AI technology being used to power cyber hacks in the region? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with that. China opposes hacking activities and fights these activities in accordance with the law. That said, we reject spreading disinformation out of political agenda. Artificial intelligence profoundly affects cybersecurity. The international community needs to step up cooperation and dialogue and set up new international rules to jointly safeguard cybersecurity. Bloomberg: Following the agreement to create a China-U.S. AI dialogue, when will the first meeting take place? Which executives from both countries will be there? Mao Ning: I’d refer you to competent authorities. AFP: The U.S. State Department has accused Zhao Fugang, the director of the overseas Chinese service center in Fiji, of paying bribes to local officials to advance China’s interests. Zhao is now banned from entering the U.S. for “significant corruption.” What is the foreign ministry’s response to that? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with that. We oppose vilification and smears against China. AFP: Japan said today it has asked China to show appropriate respect to its prime minister Sanae Takaichi. Japan said this because the Chinese foreign ministry, during its regular press conferences, often refers to the Japanese prime minister by her name alone without any title. What’s your response to Japan? Mao Ning: China has on many occasions made clear its position on the current China-Japan relations. Bloomberg: China describes its trade relationship with Europe as mutually beneficial, but European governments are seeking stronger protections. What does Beijing believe it needs to do differently to reassure them? Mao Ning: I’d refer you to China’s competent authorities for the specific question. Let me say more broadly that we hope Europe will work with China in the same direction, resolve respective concerns through dialogue and consultation, and promote the sound and steady development of China-Europe economic and trade relations. We believe this serves the common interests of both sides.
